candidate.title: RAP-RNA
candidate.scope: The single Illumina RAP-RNA schematic, specifically RNA-library construction from a RAP eluate. The far-left lncRNA/chromatin icon supplies biological context and the input carries prior RAP purification/elution history; unshown capture substeps are not reconstructed. The depicted RNA/cDNA route includes depletion of biotinylated antisense RNA probe products. DNA sequencing and protein/mass-spectrometry workflows mentioned elsewhere are outside this schematic.

states.label: Complex from RAP elution
features: Prior RAP purification enriched a known endogenous lncRNA through complementary biotinylated antisense RNA probes; associated material may accompany it.
The left icons depict a lncRNA-associated chromatin/protein complex and a bead-associated complex. They provide context for the eluate, rather than a separately drawn DNA-library branch.
The source caption calls this material an eluate even though the icon retains a bead; downstream preparation acts on the recovered RAP material.

states.label: De-crosslinked, DNase-treated RNA mixture
features: Contains endogenous RNA (purple, labeled lncRNA) and exogenous antisense RNA probes (orange).
Both drawn RNA species have a 5′P label at their left end; the probe additionally carries the blue star labeled Biotin.
Crosslinked complex architecture is removed and DNA is digested; endogenous RNA and capture-probe RNA remain substrates for library preparation.

features: Lower purple/blue hybrid remains after streptavidin depletion of biotin-bearing probe hybrids.

operations.label: Reverse crosslink and DNase digest
operations.description: Convert the recovered RAP complex into an RNA mixture by reversing crosslinks and digesting DNA. The output still contains endogenous RNA and biotinylated antisense RNA probes.
operations.mechanism: Crosslink reversal releases the complex constituents; DNase digests DNA, leaving the depicted RNA substrates.
operations.information_effect: Prior RAP selection provides the link to the known lncRNA. Physical crosslink connectivity is not carried forward as a sequenced junction in this drawing.

operations.label: Dephosphorylate and add adapters
operations.description: Dephosphorylate the RNA mixture and ligate the first adapter. Red adapter segments appear on both the endogenous RNA and the biotinylated RNA probe, so the probe remains capable of generating unwanted library products.
operations.mechanism: The labeled phosphate-bearing input is dephosphorylated and an adapter is ligated; no adapter sequence or enzyme identity is assigned.
operations.information_effect: The first adapter supplies a library-construction interface to both RNA classes; it does not itself discriminate endogenous RNA from capture-probe RNA.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Copy each adapter-bearing RNA class into cDNA. The output contains endogenous-RNA/cDNA hybrids and biotinylated probe-RNA/cDNA hybrids, rather than already purified endogenous cDNA.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription synthesizes complementary DNA from the RNA templates; RNA and cDNA remain annealed for depletion.
operations.information_effect: Sequence information passes from endogenous RNA into cDNA, but probe RNA also produces cDNA at this point.

operations.label: Wash-off probes with streptavidin
operations.description: Partition the mixed hybrids by capturing the biotinylated antisense RNA probes with streptavidin while RNA and cDNA remain annealed. Remove the probe-derived hybrid fraction and retain the endogenous-RNA/cDNA fraction for library completion.
operations.mechanism: Streptavidin binds probe biotin. Because probe RNA and its copied cDNA remain annealed, the paired cDNA is inferred to accompany the captured probe. Streptavidin serves as the affinity reagent for this separation.
operations.information_effect: Reduces exogenous probe-derived sequence noise; depletion does not by itself establish that every retained RNA is a specific or directly contacting biological partner.

operations.label: Ligate adapters and PCR amplify
operations.description: Complete preparation of the retained cDNA with a second adapter and PCR amplification, yielding the depicted double-stranded adapter-flanked cDNA library. The catalogue places cDNA purification before the second ligation; unshown purification substeps are not reconstructed.
operations.mechanism: Second-adapter ligation and PCR amplification are a single broad depicted library-finishing block.
operations.information_effect: The sequenced carrier is endogenous-RNA-derived cDNA. Each retained insert identifies an RNA sequence recovered in the RAP sample; the known purification target supplies the sample-level association. The readout includes the bait and potentially co-purifying RNAs, and this scheme alone does not distinguish direct RNA contacts from indirect association or background. DNA-chromatin mapping in the 2013 paper uses a different purified fraction.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card heading and far-left diagram title name one target, RAP-RNA. All five local operations belong to its depicted post-RAP RNA-library route. RAP is the upstream capture component represented by the input history; the card does not depict RAP-DNA, protein analysis, or differential-crosslinking alternatives as additional targets. The 2013 paper supports RAP purification plus sequencing its RNA fraction; the 2014 abstract explicitly names RAP-RNA and its RNA-RNA association readout. Neither establishes that every implementation of the RAP-RNA family uses identical preparation.
